title: Launch and baseline: what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline
focus: what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline
essential_question: What do careful readers and writers do every day, and how do I show what a text actually says?
learning_objectives: Surface what you already know and produce a no-penalty baseline.
Support your thinking with evidence from the text, a documented process, or a stated reason, rather than an unsupported answer.
Check the work against the stated success criteria and name one next step.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, or a documented process rather than a bare answer.
The learner checks the work against the criteria and identifies a next step.
materials: course notebook or an accessible digital equivalent
pencil, keyboard, or another accessible response tool
the assigned passage in print, on screen, or read aloud

text_reference.title: The Bus-Stop Library
text_reference.rights: Original Manuel Academy text. All rights reserved by Manuel Academy.
text_reference.learner_or_family_selected_texts_permitt: A facilitator may substitute a public-domain, library, licensed, or family-approved text at the same target. Record the substitution in the source record; do not paste copyrighted text into the package.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a brief accessible retrieval prompt connected to what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline. Ask the learner to recall, predict, or pose a question before any instruction.
Two minutes of word work on the vocabulary what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline requires, then one short passage read for accuracy and phrasing. Reading aloud is optional.
Introduce what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline with one short, accessible example. Say plainly that today's work is a starting picture, not a score.
Try what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline together on one easy item. Name aloud what the learner already does well.
The learner attempts what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline once on their own so today's starting point is on record.
Name one thing you already know about what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline and one thing you want help with.

student_activity: The learner attempts what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline once on their own so today's starting point is on record.
formative_check: Name one thing you already know about what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline and one thing you want help with.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may question, model on a separate example, name a criterion, restate directions, or point to where an idea is unclear. The tutor must not draft, dictate, outline, complete, reword, or supply sentences for the learner's assessed essay or extended response.
fixed_answer_protection: Fixed-answer items and their keys are scorer-visible only. The tutor surface, the learner surface, and any hint path must not expose, restate, or narrow toward a fixed answer before the learner responds. Feedback after a response addresses reasoning, not the key.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated target, the accuracy of the reading or writing move, the quality of the evidence or reasoning, and the revision. Accept any approach that meets the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, character, or diagnosis from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: If the barrier is reading the words rather than what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline, drop to the word or phrase level, reread the line, then return. Do not reteach what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline while decoding is the actual obstacle.
Return to the smallest prerequisite what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline depends on, model it once with a text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Accept the thinking, then require the learner to locate the words in the text that support it. If none exist, treat that as the finding and revise the claim.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline, and do not assign remediation the evidence does not justify.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short retrieval check in a later session.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: text too hard for the grades 2-3 band
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Swap to a shorter text at the same target rather than lowering the target. Record the swap as an access decision, not as a mastery result.
Require accurate independent application of what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline plus an explanation on a second, later occasion before recording mastery.

mastery.separation: The two occasions must be separated by time, by text, or by representation.
evidence_types: text-marked or annotated reading response
written response with cited evidence
oral or written explanation of reasoning
a revision that shows the learner acted on criteria
transfer to an unfamiliar text or task
mastery.rule: A single correct answer never establishes mastery. Guided success is recorded as guided evidence and is weighted below independent evidence. A pacing concern is not a mastery failure.

mastery_rule: Do not record mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent evidence plus an explanation, transfer, or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time, text, or representation. Guided success is recorded as guided evidence only.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, labeled illustration, chart, or short captioned clip supporting what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the target, completion state, evidence type, whether the evidence was guided or independent, and the next instructional step. Do not expose raw responses, private reflections, voice recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of what strong readers and writers do, and a no-penalty baseline in everyday reading, conversation, or writing. No purchase, account, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

title: Writing plan and draft: planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you
focus: planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you
essential_question: What do careful readers and writers do every day, and how do I show what a text actually says?
learning_objectives: Plan and draft writing that carries planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you.
Support your thinking with evidence from the text, a documented process, or a stated reason, rather than an unsupported answer.
Check the work against the stated success criteria and name one next step.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, or a documented process rather than a bare answer.
The learner checks the work against the criteria and identifies a next step.
materials: course notebook or an accessible digital equivalent
pencil, keyboard, or another accessible response tool
the assigned passage in print, on screen, or read aloud

text_reference.description: The learner's own draft. No published text is required for this session.
text_reference.learner_or_family_selected_texts_permitt: A facilitator may substitute a public-domain, library, licensed, or family-approved text at the same target. Record the substitution in the source record; do not paste copyrighted text into the package.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a brief accessible retrieval prompt connected to planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you. Ask the learner to recall, predict, or pose a question before any instruction.
Two minutes of word work on the vocabulary planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you requires, then one short passage read for accuracy and phrasing. Reading aloud is optional.
Show a plan for the writing task, then draft the opening in front of the learner and think aloud while choosing.
Build the learner's plan together: what it is about, what goes first, and what the reader needs.
The learner drafts from their own plan. The tutor may question and prompt but writes none of the learner's text.
What is your writing about in one sentence, and what comes first?

student_activity: The learner drafts from their own plan. The tutor may question and prompt but writes none of the learner's text.
formative_check: What is your writing about in one sentence, and what comes first?
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may question, model on a separate example, name a criterion, restate directions, or point to where an idea is unclear. The tutor must not draft, dictate, outline, complete, reword, or supply sentences for the learner's assessed essay or extended response.
fixed_answer_protection: Fixed-answer items and their keys are scorer-visible only. The tutor surface, the learner surface, and any hint path must not expose, restate, or narrow toward a fixed answer before the learner responds. Feedback after a response addresses reasoning, not the key.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated target, the accuracy of the reading or writing move, the quality of the evidence or reasoning, and the revision. Accept any approach that meets the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, character, or diagnosis from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: If the barrier is reading the words rather than planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you, drop to the word or phrase level, reread the line, then return. Do not reteach planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you while decoding is the actual obstacle.
Return to the smallest prerequisite planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you depends on, model it once with a text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Accept the thinking, then require the learner to locate the words in the text that support it. If none exist, treat that as the finding and revise the claim.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you, and do not assign remediation the evidence does not justify.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short retrieval check in a later session.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: text too hard for the grades 2-3 band
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Swap to a shorter text at the same target rather than lowering the target. Record the swap as an access decision, not as a mastery result.
Require accurate independent application of planning three sentences about one reading habit that helps you plus an explanation on a second, later occasion before recording mastery.

written response with cited evidence
oral or written explanation of reasoning
a revision that shows the learner acted on criteria
transfer to an unfamiliar text or task

A no-audio path is provided: any listening task may be replaced with the printed transcript or a written script.
Where media is used it must carry captions and a transcript, or it must not be used.
Directions are chunked to one action at a time, with a worked example available for every task.
Typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, dictated-to-scribe, or pointed responses are accepted whenever the standard does not name the mode.

Reduced copying, extended time, hidden timers, movement breaks, high-contrast print, larger type, keyboard access, and low-distraction settings are available on request and are not recorded as failures.
A private presentation alternative exists for every speaking or presenting task; no learner voice or video recording is ever required.
The learning target is preserved while quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode is adjusted.

speaking_and_listening_alternatives.private_presentation_alternative: Any presenting, reporting, or discussion turn may be delivered privately to one adult, submitted in writing, typed, or displayed silently.
speaking_and_listening_alternatives.no_audio_path: Listening tasks may be completed from a printed transcript or script. No task requires hearing audio.
speaking_and_listening_alternatives.recording_is_opt_in: Where a standard names audio recording, the learner may satisfy it with a written script plus a silent visual display, or with an adult-read recording. Learner voice is never required and is never stored without explicit guardian opt-in.

safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about reading difficulty, spelling, handwriting, speech, accent, or pace.
A pause, a break, or a change of response mode is never recorded as a failure.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; a fictionalized, analytical, or private-safe alternative is always acceptable.
Offer an alternate text or a private response when content is personally sensitive, and teach difficult history and literature with accuracy, context, and dignity.
Parent-facing summaries show the target, completion, evidence type, and next step, never raw private reflections, raw responses, or diagnosis language.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, labeled illustration, chart, or short captioned clip supporting correcting one section and publishing the year-end portfolio.
media.fallback: The same information is provided as readable text, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No learner is disadvantaged by declining media.

not_required_to_store: the learner's raw essay or extended written response text
persistence.note: The runtime may evaluate an extended response in session and persist only the evidence descriptors above. No part of this course requires storing a learner's raw essay text.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the target, completion state, evidence type, whether the evidence was guided or independent, and the next instructional step. Do not expose raw responses, private reflections, voice recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of correcting one section and publishing the year-end portfolio in everyday reading, conversation, or writing. No purchase, account, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
